details: On July 13, 2026, U.S. President Donald Trump announced the reinstatement of a naval blockade on Iran in the Strait of Hormuz, declaring that the U.S. would charge a 20% fee on eligible cargo transiting the critical waterway. This move by the U.S. escalates tensions following recent mutual attacks with Iran. The U.S. military confirmed it would resume the blockade of Iranian ports on July 14, 2026, warning of force if ships do not comply, though humanitarian shipments will be allowed. The announcement has significantly contributed to rising oil prices.
title: US Restores Iran Blockade, Levies 20% Fee on Hormuz Shipping

details: On July 14, 2026, the United Arab Emirates reported that Iranian cruise missiles struck two Emirati oil tankers, Mombasa B and Al Bahiya, in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one mariner and injuring eight others. This attack occurred as the United States carried out its third consecutive night of strikes against Iranian targets, including port cities and islands in Iran. The ongoing military actions intensify the Middle East conflict, further impacting shipping safety and leading to a rise in global oil prices.
title: Iran Hits Two UAE Tankers Amid US Strikes in Strait of Hormuz
